Chapter 207: 0204 Sanguosha's Exclusive Theme Song

The Sanguosha National Collegiate League currently only featured 1v1 and 3v3 modes.

Each participating team had a minimum of three members and a maximum of five.

The current system was a double-elimination tournament, with a draw dividing teams into groups A and B.

Each group would play three 1v1 matches. A player could only play one game and could not participate again. Winning two out of three games earned 1 point.

The group would also play two 3v3 matches, with each win earning 1 point, for a total of 2 points.

The team with more points would advance to the winner's bracket.

"Player Xue Lin from South China University of Technology bans Zhen Ji."

"Player Liu Ruiqiang from Xi'an Jiao-tong bans Lu Xun. He picks Huang Yueying."

"Will Xue Lin pick Diao Chan? No. He picked Gan Ning!"

In the third row of the audience, Wang Ruodu couldn't help but laugh when he saw the character selections.

If Huang Yueying couldn't burst Gan Ning down in one or two waves, she was in for a slow and torturous defeat.

Wang Ruodu had been obsessed with StarCraft in high school, frequenting the various internet cafes outside of school. As the college entrance exams approached, he decided he should study, so he crammed for two months and got into Peking University.

He had barely scraped into Peking University and was assigned to environmental engineering. He studied hard during his freshman year and successfully transferred to the mathematics department.

Then he started gaming even more wildly, even joining a professional team and fighting his way from the Chinese circuit to the international stage.

As his grades were at the bottom of his class, he felt this couldn't go on.

So last year, he spent three months reviewing and successfully got into Peking University's financial mathematics master's program.

After securing his spot as a graduate student, Wang Ruodu, who occasionally played Sanguosha, discovered that his own university's team had been eliminated in the top eight.

How embarrassing!

He planned to participate in the second National Collegiate League to bring a championship trophy back for Peking University. He was currently writing a Sanguosha competition tutorial.

"Sanguosha: The Path of Kings" was written by him...

"It's over." Wang Ruodu muttered to himself while staring at the big screen.

As he watched, after her initial burst, although Huang Yueying had reduced Gan Ning to two health and was fully equipped herself, Gan Ning was battered but not beaten.

Apart from dismantling the -1 Horse, Gan Ning didn't even bother with Huang Yueying's other equipment. Whenever he got a black card, he would use it to dismantle Huang Yueying's hand cards.

Gradually, Gan Ning recovered to three health, with both an Attack and a Dodge in his hand.

Meanwhile, Huang Yueying, despite being at full health, was always short on cards.

Finally, Huang Yueying was ground down and defeated.

*Clap clap clap!*

The entire venue erupted in applause, mixed with some laughter.

Wang Ruodu watched all three 1v1 matches and wrote in his small notebook: "These Sanguosha players don't pay much attention to card counting or probability calculation..."

Experts from prestigious schools like Tsinghua, Zhejiang University, Shanghai Jiao Tong, and Fudan had also come to observe the competition. Some of them hadn't played Sanguosha before and only started paying attention to the game after hearing their own schools had been eliminated.

By the second Sanguosha Collegiate League, the scene would probably be packed with master players!

After Group A's matches concluded, a cosplay performance of Shu Kingdom generals began.

Then, after Group B's matches, there was a cosplay performance of Wu Kingdom generals.

Following that was the first match of the loser's bracket.

As noon approached, the host Huang Xi said, "Let's welcome the singer of 'The Wind Rises,' Bian Guanyue, to perform for us the exclusive theme song for Sanguosha..."

JJ Lin's "Cao Cao" and Tank's "Romance of the Three Kingdoms" were both set to be released next month.

Chen Guiliang would never dare to plagiarize these two songs.

It would be an absolute train wreck.

But Chen Guiliang did want to invite JJ Lin to be a spokesperson for Sanguosha.

Neither Chen Guiliang nor Xie Yang had a clear grasp of how commercial endorsements worked last year. Now, they basically understood that the prices for these things fluctuated wildly.

It all depended on how you negotiated!

For example, the popular young actor Huang Lei asked for a 1.8 million yuan endorsement deal. It was eventually negotiated down to 1.2 million, but the advertiser thought it was too high and decided to look for someone else. A few days later, Huang Lei's agent actively reached out, lowering the price to 800,000 yuan.

The advertiser said they still needed to consider it, so Huang Lei's agent spread the word through an acquaintance, hinting that if they wanted to sign, five or six hundred thousand yuan would also be acceptable.

From 1.8 million down to 500,000, and it was Huang Lei's agent who actively lowered the price time and time again...

There were also cases of advertisers raising the price in reverse.

For example, the boss of a certain menswear brand was set on having Chen Daoming as their spokesperson, but Chen Daoming stubbornly refused to do commercials. The advertising agency advised the client to pick another celebrity, but the client would only accept Chen Daoming.

In the end, Chen Daoming, who had repeatedly claimed he wouldn't do commercials, cheerfully endorsed the menswear brand. Because they simply offered too much, raising the price all the way to 26 million!

With the right negotiation strategy, JJ Lin's non-exclusive endorsement could be secured for 2 million yuan.

This was because celebrities from Hong Kong and Taiwan had been overvalued in recent years, often inflating their asking prices several times over. Anyone who believed them was a sucker!

Bian Guanyue had already changed into a historical costume backstage and gracefully walked out as the song's intro began.

Fearing a clash with "Cao Cao" and "Romance of the Three Kingdoms," which song should he choose?

"A white-robed figure glides over the river, a sip of wine brings fleeting clarity. Riding the dragon on the wind, old dreams of crimson glaze and jade palaces, a chain of burning camps..."

The original singer of this song was an online singer and Tongji University graduate, Yin Yuqiong.

Later, Bella Yao bought the copyright and re-recorded it.

Sorry, Pony Ma, I've ripped off another one of your future online game theme songs.

Chen Guiliang only changed two characters in the lyrics, changing "wolf smoke and beacon fires fill the banners" to "wolf smoke and beacon fires cover the land."

"Wow, a beauty! So much prettier than the female host!"

"She's on the same level as the Zhen Ji cosplayer."

"Quiet, listen to the song!"

Bian Guanyue had never performed publicly before, not even showing her face for "The Wind Rises."

At this moment, a close-up of her appeared on the big screen, drawing gasps of admiration from the audience.

Her historical costume, the beautiful Chinese-style melody and lyrics, perfectly struck a chord with these Sanguosha fans.

This song might not have caused a stir elsewhere.

But played here, at a Sanguosha tournament, reaching the ears of Sanguosha players, it was like hearing heavenly music!

When she first came on stage, Bian Guanyue was a bit reserved, but she loosened up as she sang.

She had thought she would resist public performance, but unexpectedly, she found herself thoroughly enjoying the atmosphere.

This was her stage.

"A broken halberd sinks in the sand, autumn waters dim, petals fall as my lord departs... The grass and trees on Changban Slope reek of blood, a dream of the Cangjiang River in a mirror's reflection..."

The more Bian Guanyue sang, the more engrossed she became, completely immersed in the song.

*Clap clap clap clap!*

Thunderous applause.

After she finished singing, Bian Guanyue became nervous again, forgetting to bow to the audience before running off the stage.

Her heart was pounding violently.

A nitpicking audience member said, "Is this just a pile of fancy lyrics? What does 'yipin qianjin' mean? The precious daughter of a first-rank official?"

There were quite a few knowledgeable people in the audience, and someone nearby immediately said, "'Yipin qianjin' refers to fame and fortune. This line and the one before it are both allusions to a poem by Fan Zhongyan. The original poem was related to the Three Kingdoms."

"Damn, I guess I can't even understand lyrics if I'm not cultured," that person grumbled.

As the morning's events concluded, people left in groups, discussing the matches, the cosplayers, and the song. With their ticket stubs, they could get a free set meal at the Peking University cafeteria.

People also asked each other which server they played on in "Sanguosha OL." If they happened to be on the same one, they would exchange contact information on the spot and make plans to play together.

A staff member stood outside shouting, "Everyone can receive one Sanguosha throw pillow. Please do not take more than one."

You could get a pillow too?

This was a pleasant surprise, and the audience members hurried to line up.

A staff member doubling as a photographer immediately took pictures, then took out a card reader, plugged it into a computer, and started a live photo and text broadcast on 17173.com and the Sanguosha Tieba forum.

Netizens watching from their computers were green with envy.

"Is Youke really not trying to make money? A 15 yuan ticket includes lunch and a free pillow."

"Where can I buy this pillow?"

"The official Sanguosha Taobao store. It's been listed for over two months."

"Was that song just now called 'Dragon Rider's Chant'? The singer is so beautiful, too bad we can only see the lyrics."

"The song is pinned on the Tieba homepage. You can also download it from 9tian music."

"I just listened to it, the lyrics and music are incredible. Our President Chen is so talented, who knew he could also write songs."

"President Chen already wrote 'The Wind Rises.' You guys are just finding out?"

"Chen Guiliang wrote 'The Wind Rises'? No way!"

Chen Guiliang had already gone backstage, where Bian Guanyue was chatting with the host, players, and cosplayers.

"President Chen!"

"Hello, Boss Chen!"

Everyone stopped their conversations and came over to shake Chen Guiliang's hand.

Chen Guiliang said, "Thank you all for your hard work. Let's go eat together."

These people had special meals. They would also eat in a cafeteria, but it was arranged in a different one. This was partly to show them special consideration, and partly to prevent them from being bothered by the audience.

Bian Guanyue had changed back into her everyday clothes and now appeared especially energetic and confident.

"How did you feel, performing publicly for the first time?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue smiled and said, "When I first went on stage, my palms were all sweaty. I was so nervous, I even went off-key on the second line. But it got better, and it became smoother as I sang. It's just that after I finished and heard the audience applaud, I got nervous all over again."

"That's just because you lack stage experience. You'll get used to it after a few more times," Chen Guiliang comforted her.

Bian Guanyue asked, "Back when you were in your third year of high school, with so many reporters at the school, weren't you nervous on stage by yourself?"

Chen Guiliang boasted, "I'm a natural showman. The bigger the crowd, the more excited I get."

"You're still the amazing one," Bian Guanyue said with sincere admiration.

What natural showman?

Everyone gets stage fright. Chen Guiliang had just trained himself out of it by living a second life.

Bian Guanyue said half-jokingly, "How about I go audition for Super Girl next year?"

Chen Guiliang was encouraging but also reminded her, "Go if you want to. But with Jane Zhang as a precedent, the contracts for the next season of Super Girl will be extremely strict. If you're not willing to sign with EE-Media, you'll probably be eliminated in the regional qualifiers. It won't matter how well you sing."

"That's perfect then. I'll just participate in a few rounds for the experience," Bian Guanyue said, feeling relieved to hear this.

She had been worried that participating in Super Girl would interfere with her studies.

Bian Guanyue was a good student who won a scholarship every year.

Afternoon.

First, the fourth-place winner was announced: Shandong University.

Third place: Sichuan University.

Xi'an Jiao-tong and South China University of Technology, who had faced off in the very first match that morning, met again in the final.

South China University of Technology defeated Xi'an Jiao-tong to win the first-ever championship.

Chen Guiliang personally went on stage to present them with their awards.

Don't think that a 50,000 yuan champion's prize was too shabby. In 2005, the prize money for the Warcraft, StarCraft, and CS champions in the CEG league was only 30,000 yuan. The Warcraft champion at the WCG China finals only won 20,000 yuan.

The 50,000 yuan prize that Chen Guiliang gave to the entire Sanguosha champion team was already far higher than other competitions.

The five members of the champion team were thrilled as they received their prize.

They were very lucky, because this was only the first tournament, and many master players had not participated.

(End of Chapter)
